name: weightedVar
title: Weighted variance and weighted standard deviation

origin.description: Computes a weighted variance of a numeric vector.
origin.usage:
weightedVar(x, w = NULL, idxs = NULL, na.rm = FALSE, center = NULL,
  ...)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A vector of type integer, numeric, or logical.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: A vector of weights the same length as x. Negative weights are treated as zero weights. Default value is equal weight to all values.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A vector indicating subset of elements to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: center
arguments.text: Optional numeric scalar specifying the center location of the data. If NULL, it is estimated from data.

origin.details: The estimator is the unbiased estimator of Hmisc::wtd.var: sum(w * (x - center)^2) / (sum(w) - 1). If center is NULL it is sum(w * x) / sum(w) after weights that are missing or not strictly positive have been handled. A positive infinite weight keeps only the infinite-weight observations and resets those weights to 1. If na.rm is FALSE, a missing value in x or w gives NA. If na.rm is TRUE, points whose x is missing are skipped, including a point where both are missing. A missing weight paired with a present x still gives NA.
origin.value: A numeric scalar. If fewer than two observations remain, the result is NA in the storage mode of x.

translation.description: Computes a weighted variance of a numeric vector.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: One-dimensional numeric vector. This is x in R. A matrix is read in column-major order, as R stores it.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: A vector of weights the same length as x. None gives every original element weight 1, and that vector is not subset by idxs. A weight that is not strictly positive is dropped, including negative infinity. A missing weight that remains makes the result R's NA.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: 1-based vector indicating the subset of elements to operate over. None means no subsetting. Integer, numeric, and logical subscripts follow base R, including zero, negative exclusion, and logical recycling.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, points whose x is missing are skipped. This is na.rm in R. The default is False.

arguments.name: center
arguments.text: Optional numeric center. None estimates sum(w * x) / sum(w) after the weight filter. A supplied center is subtracted as R would, including recycling.

translation.details: The divisor is sum(w) - 1, so the variance is negative when the remaining weights sum to less than 1. The center is not weightedMean: that function keeps a negative weight, and this one drops every weight that is not strictly positive. With w omitted, idxs subsets x only, and a false na_rm recycles the original weights of length length(x).
translation.value: A float64 scalar. Fewer than two remaining observations, or a missing x or w that is not dropped, is R's NA. An indeterminate arithmetic result is a plain NaN.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.weightedvar import weightedVar

weightedVar(np.arange(1, 11, dtype=float))
